narrativeReportMd:
# AllergyIntolerance R4→R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`AllergyIntolerance` keeps the same resource identity in R6, but several local element-level changes are breaking at the wire format or cross-version validation level. The highest-impact issues are the `lastOccurrence` to `lastReactionOccurrence` rename, `reaction.manifestation` changing from `CodeableConcept` to `CodeableReference(Observation)`, and `type` changing from a primitive required-bound `code` to a preferred-bound `CodeableConcept`.

## Scope
The analysis used the local R4 and R6 core StructureDefinitions plus directly related local terminology, ConceptMaps, the R6 `CodeableReference` datatype, package indexes, and package metadata. Inherited `Resource`/`DomainResource`/`Element` changes are excluded from `findings[]`.

## Main migration themes
The main migration work is structural, not cardinality-driven: existing JSON property shapes must change for `type` and `reaction.manifestation`, and the renamed last-reaction date element must be remapped. R6 also widens representable content through `CodeableReference`, `CodeableConcept`, a likely new `verificationStatus` code, relaxed clinical-status constraints, and an added `Organization` recorder target; those create R6-to-R4 loss or validation failures.

## Highest-impact findings
High-impact findings are AllergyIntolerance:ELEMENT_PRESENCE_OR_IDENTITY:AllergyIntolerance.lastOccurrence:6bc377, AllergyIntolerance:TYPE_DOMAIN:AllergyIntolerance.reaction.manifestation:5ab95c, and AllergyIntolerance:TYPE_DOMAIN:AllergyIntolerance.type:d86f8f. All three can make valid R4 instances fail R6 validation when the affected optional element is present, and all three can break generated models, serializers, FHIRPath expressions, and downstream business logic.

## Findings requiring human review
Terminology confidence is limited for AllergyIntolerance:TERMINOLOGY_BINDING:AllergyIntolerance.verificationStatus:0ef842 because no local R6 expansion or terminology.hl7.org CodeSystem artifact was available, though the R6 StructureDefinition short text and ConceptMap both indicate the `presumed` code. The clinical-status constraint removal in AllergyIntolerance:VALUE_CONSTRAINT:AllergyIntolerance.clinicalStatus:203225 also deserves review because the computable constraint was removed while guidance moved into comments and appears to account for negated allergy codes.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Most changes have plausible clinical modeling goals, but several could have been made less disruptive by retaining the R4 element or shape for one release, adding optional parallel elements, or using extensions/profiles for the expanded cases. These alternatives reduce migration burden but can preserve ambiguity or duplicate data.

## Follow-up analysis
Separate analyses should cover the affected SearchParameters, the `CodeableReference` datatype itself, terminology expansions from terminology.hl7.org, and any removed AllergyIntolerance extension artifacts.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `AllergyIntolerance` has material local breaking changes despite stable resource identity. The top migration concerns are remapping `lastOccurrence`, converting `reaction.manifestation` to `CodeableReference`, and converting primitive `type` values into `CodeableConcept`; the main uncertainty is terminology expansion confirmation for verification-status codes.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration is mainly a JSON/model-shape problem plus an R6-to-R4 lossiness problem. R4-to-R6 transforms should rename `lastOccurrence`, wrap `reaction.manifestation` CodeableConcepts under `CodeableReference.concept`, and wrap `type` primitive codes as CodeableConcept codings. R6-to-R4 transforms need policies for Observation-backed manifestations, non-value-set `type` CodeableConcepts, `verificationStatus=presumed`, missing or otherwise R4-invalid `clinicalStatus` combinations, and `recorder` references to `Organization`.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for structural changes because both StructureDefinitions are present and directly comparable. Confidence is medium for exact terminology membership of R6 terminology.hl7.org systems because expansions and R6 CodeSystem artifacts for allergyintolerance clinical/verification status were not available locally; the `presumed` finding is supported by the R6 StructureDefinition short text and ConceptMap rather than by a local expansion.

findings.title: AllergyIntolerance.lastOccurrence was replaced by lastReactionOccurrence

semanticText.short: Date(/time) of last known occurrence of a reaction
semanticText.definition: Represents the date and/or time of the last known occurrence of a reaction event.
semanticText.comment: This date may be replicated by one of the Onset of Reaction dates. Where a textual representation of the date of last occurrence is required e.g. 'In Childhood, '10 years ago' the Comment element should be used.

oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, the last reaction date is serialized as `lastOccurrence`.

newState.summary: R6 has optional `lastReactionOccurrence` as `dateTime` and no `lastOccurrence` element.

semanticText.short: Date(/time) of last known occurrence of a reaction
semanticText.definition: Represents the date and/or time of the last known occurrence of a reaction event.
semanticText.comment: This date may be replicated by one of the Onset of Reaction dates. Where a textual representation of the date of last occurrence is required e.g. 'In Childhood, '10 years ago' the AllergyIntolerance.note element should be used.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 preserves the same dateTime semantics but changes the element identity and JSON property name to `lastReactionOccurrence`.

facts.note: The old element id is absent from the R6 snapshot.
The new element has matching cardinality, type, short text, and definition.
SearchParameters are out of scope as findings but confirm the rename pattern.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The old and new elements share the same parent, cardinality, `dateTime` type, short text, and definition. The new name is a more explicit form of the old date's definition.

impact.impactRationaleMd: A valid R4 instance containing `lastOccurrence` uses a property that R6 does not define, so strict R6 validation or generated R6 models will reject or drop it. Conversely, an R6 instance containing `lastReactionOccurrence` is not directly representable in R4 without renaming the property back.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The value can affect clinical review of recency and allergy-list display, though it is optional and does not by itself change the causative substance or status.

justification.inferredGoal: Clarify that the date is the last known occurrence of a reaction, not the last occurrence of the AllergyIntolerance resource itself.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain `lastOccurrence` in the base resource and clarify that it means the last known reaction occurrence, rather than renaming the element.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of making the date's meaning clearer is reasonable, but the computable definition shows the same cardinality, datatype, and clinical meaning. Because FHIR JSON property names are not aliases, the rename directly invalidates R4 instances that contain `lastOccurrence`. Retaining the old name with clearer short text, definition, comments, and search documentation would meet most of the clarity goal while preserving existing data, so the base break looks probably avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would keep `AllergyIntolerance.lastOccurrence` as the element name and update its narrative to say explicitly that it is the last known occurrence of a reaction. If R6 also introduced `lastReactionOccurrence` as a parallel field, it would need consistency rules and would risk two same-resource date representations persisting indefinitely; simply retaining the old element avoids that duplication at the cost of living with a nonoptimal legacy name.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 instances with low implementation burden, but leaves a less precise legacy name; adding a second alias field would create duplicate date representations.

evidence.quote: Date(/time) of last known occurrence of a reaction

evidence.detail: R6 defines `lastReactionOccurrence` as 0..1 `dateTime` and the R6 snapshot has no `lastOccurrence` element.
evidence.quote: Date(/time) of last known occurrence of a reaction

evidence.detail: Related SearchParameters use the old and new element names respectively.

examples.examplesMd: Examples are minimal fragments showing the property-name incompatibility; complete production instances may include additional status, code, and reaction data.

findings.narrativeMd: `lastOccurrence` is effectively renamed to `lastReactionOccurrence`. The clinical meaning appears stable, but the element id and serialized JSON property changed. This breaks strict validators, generated model fields, FHIRPath expressions, database columns, and API clients that still read or write the R4 name.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances that contain `lastOccurrence` become invalid or at least non-conformant under R6 because R6 has no such element. R6 instances with `lastReactionOccurrence` cannot be sent to an R4 endpoint without renaming the element back. The migration is structurally simple and lossless for the value itself.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Rename `AllergyIntolerance.lastOccurrence` to `AllergyIntolerance.lastReactionOccurrence` during R4→R6 conversion and reverse it for R6→R4. Update generated classes, serializers, FHIRPath, search code, database mappings, and tests that reference `lastOccurrence` or the old `last-date` search parameter.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The clearer name could have been introduced less disruptively by retaining `lastOccurrence` and deprecating it, but base FHIR resources generally do not support aliases. Because the semantic value is unchanged, this is probably a clarity-driven rename rather than a clinically necessary representation change.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `lastOccurrence` was not broadened or clarified in place; it was replaced by `lastReactionOccurrence` while preserving the same cardinality, datatype, short text, and definition. A generated R4 client, FHIRPath rule, database mapping, or strict validator that still emits `lastOccurrence` will not match the R6 element name, even though the value itself can be migrated losslessly. Because this looks primarily like a naming cleanup on a clinically relevant date, the break is disproportionate unless there is stronger standards rationale than the supplied artifacts show.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition has `AllergyIntolerance.lastOccurrence` 0..1 `dateTime` with definition 'date and/or time of the last known occurrence of a reaction event'.
R6 StructureDefinition has `AllergyIntolerance.lastReactionOccurrence` 0..1 `dateTime` with the same short and definition, and no `lastOccurrence` element.
The current finding examples align with the primary StructureDefinition evidence: the JSON property name changes while the value semantics remain stable.
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 AllergyIntolerance is FMM 3/trial-use, so it is not under a normative freeze, but it is mature enough that a wire-name break for an established clinical summary element needs a clear benefit. The FMM context increases concern here because the apparent goal could mostly be met through clearer wording.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 instance containing `lastOccurrence` uses a property R6 does not define; generated models, FHIRPath, serializers, and reverse R6-to-R4 exchange also need explicit renaming.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Yes. R6 could have kept `lastOccurrence` as the base element name and clarified that it means last known reaction occurrence. Adding a parallel alias would create duplicate fields, but simply retaining the old wire name with better definitions would preserve existing instances at low apparent cost.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing report correctly treats this as a high-impact hard shape/name break and identifies a credible less-breaking base design.

findings.title: reaction.manifestation changed from CodeableConcept to CodeableReference(Observation)

oldState.summary: R4 manifestation is required within each reaction and repeats as `CodeableConcept`.

binding.description: Clinical symptoms and/or signs that are observed or associated with an Adverse Reaction Event.

semanticText.short: Clinical symptoms/signs associated with the Event
semanticText.definition: Clinical symptoms and/or signs that are observed or associated with the adverse reaction event.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 records each reaction manifestation as a directly embedded CodeableConcept.

newState.summary: R6 manifestation remains 1..* but each item is a `CodeableReference` that may contain a concept or reference an Observation.

binding.description: Clinical symptoms and/or signs that are observed or associated with an Adverse Reaction Event.

semanticText.short: Clinical symptoms/signs associated with the Event
semanticText.definition: Clinical symptoms and/or signs that are observed or associated with the adverse reaction event.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 uses `CodeableReference`, so coded manifestations move under `manifestation.concept`, and manifestations can alternatively point to an `Observation`.

facts.note: SearchParameter changes are supporting context only.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The element id, path, cardinality, binding, short text, and definition were retained, while the declared type changed.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The JSON shape of every reaction manifestation changed. A direct R4 `CodeableConcept` item is not a valid R6 `CodeableReference` item unless wrapped under `concept`, and R6 Observation references have no native R4 element to hold them.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Manifestations are clinically meaningful symptoms/signs used in allergy review, displays, and possibly decision support; losing or misreading them can affect interpretation of adverse reaction history.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow a manifestation to be represented either as a coded concept or as a reference to supporting Observation evidence.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `reaction.manifestation` as `CodeableConcept` and add a separate optional Observation reference path for evidence-linked manifestations.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred R6 goal is strong: manifestations may need to be represented either as coded symptoms/signs or as references to Observation evidence. A parallel reference element would be less disruptive for R4-coded manifestations, but it would duplicate the manifestation concept and require rules for whether a code, a reference, or both are authoritative. Those material model and interoperability tradeoffs make the alternative only partial, so the breaking move to the single `CodeableReference` pattern is probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could retain the R4 `CodeableConcept` shape and add something like `reaction.manifestationObservation` or a choice/companion element for Observation references. That would let old JSON validate unchanged, but producers and consumers would need to handle two places for the same manifestation, queries would need to combine code and reference paths, and deprecated coded-only representations might never disappear. Conversion tooling or extensions help migration but are not the base-design alternative being counted here.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves common coded R4 manifestations but creates two same-resource representations for one clinical fact, with validation, search, and precedence ambiguity.

evidence.detail: R4 declares the element as `CodeableConcept` with cardinality 1..*.
R6 declares the element as `CodeableReference` with targetProfile `Observation` and cardinality 1..*.
CodeableReference carries either `concept` as CodeableConcept or `reference` as Reference.

examples.examplesMd: R4 coded manifestations can be migrated losslessly by wrapping the old CodeableConcept in `concept`. R6 reference-only manifestations require either dereferencing and summarizing the Observation or preserving the reference in an extension when converting to R4.

findings.narrativeMd: `reaction.manifestation` kept the same path but changed datatype from `CodeableConcept` to `CodeableReference`. This is a direct serialization and code-generation break because R4 clients expect manifestation items to have `coding`/`text` directly, while R6 clients expect `concept` or `reference` children.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 instance with a normal coded manifestation is not valid R6 unless transformed to `manifestation.concept`. R6 instances that use the new Observation reference capability are valid R6 but cannot be faithfully represented in R4's CodeableConcept-only field without loss or extension. Generated classes and search logic must also distinguish code-based and reference-based manifestations.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R4→R6, wrap every `reaction.manifestation` CodeableConcept as `{"concept": <old CodeableConcept>}`. For R6→R4, map `concept` back to the R4 item shape; if `reference` is present, decide whether to dereference the Observation into a code/text summary, store a cross-version extension, or flag the instance for manual review. Add tests for coded-only, reference-only, and combined CodeableReference cases.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change supports richer evidence links but was not wire-compatible. A parallel optional reference element would have been easier for R4 clients to ignore, but `CodeableReference` avoids duplicate concepts and follows an R6 modeling pattern used elsewhere.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `reaction.manifestation` keeps its path and 1..* cardinality but changes each item from a direct `CodeableConcept` to a `CodeableReference` that can carry either `concept` or an `Observation` reference. Existing coded R4 manifestations therefore require a wrapper transform, and R6 reference-only manifestations cannot be faithfully reduced to R4 without dereferencing, summarizing, or preserving extension/provenance data. The migration is real and clinically important, but the R6 design goal of linking manifestations to Observation evidence is strong and a separate companion reference path would split one clinical fact across two representations.
keyEvidence: R4 `AllergyIntolerance.reaction.manifestation` is 1..* `CodeableConcept` with example binding to clinical findings.
R6 `AllergyIntolerance.reaction.manifestation` is 1..* `CodeableReference` with targetProfile `Observation`, while the binding, short, and definition remain materially stable.
R6 `CodeableReference` contains optional `concept` (`CodeableConcept`) and optional `reference` (`Reference`) children.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use raises the burden because reaction manifestations are central clinical content, but it does not preclude a structural change when the new representation solves a real modeling problem. Here the maturity context makes the break worth calling out, not enough to make it disproportionate.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: a direct R4 manifestation item with `coding`/`text` is not the R6 `CodeableReference` shape unless wrapped under `concept`; additionally, R6 `Observation` references create R6-to-R4 loss.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Partial. R6 could have retained the coded `manifestation` field and added a separate optional Observation reference element, but that would create duplicate/competing representations, precedence questions, and split search/query behavior. The single `CodeableReference` path is more disruptive but more coherent.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing high-impact assessment and partial less-breaking alternative judgment match the independent path-level assessment.

findings.title: AllergyIntolerance.type changed from required primitive code to preferred CodeableConcept

oldState.summary: R4 `type` is an optional primitive `code` with a required binding to allergy/intolerance.

binding.description: Identification of the underlying physiological mechanism for a Reaction Risk.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: Local CodeSystem artifacts list the same two R4/R6 codes, `allergy` and `intolerance`, but no expansion was available.

semanticText.definition: Identification of the underlying physiological mechanism for the reaction risk.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 serializes `type` as a primitive string code such as `"allergy"`.

newState.summary: R6 `type` is an optional `CodeableConcept` with a preferred binding to the same value set canonical.

binding.description: Identification of the underlying physiological mechanism for a Reaction Risk.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The R6 local CodeSystem still has `allergy` and `intolerance`; the binding is weaker and allows other codings/text as preferred-bound CodeableConcept content.

semanticText.definition: Identification of the underlying physiological mechanism for the reaction risk.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 serializes `type` as a CodeableConcept, for example with `coding.system` and `coding.code`, and the binding is no longer required.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The same element id and clinical definition were retained, but the datatype and binding strength changed.

impact.impactRationaleMd: A present R4 primitive `type` value is not the R6 object shape, so strict validators and generated R6 clients will reject it. R6 can also carry a CodeableConcept with only text or non-value-set codings, which has no lossless R4 primitive-code representation and may fail R4's required binding.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The element distinguishes allergy from intolerance where known. Incorrect conversion can affect display, filtering, and some clinical rules, though the element remains optional.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow more nuanced or externally coded expression of the underlying mechanism while acknowledging that allergy/intolerance boundaries can be uncertain.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain primitive `type` for the legacy allergy/intolerance distinction and add an optional CodeableConcept detail element for richer mechanism coding.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal is plausible because the R4 comments acknowledge clinical ambiguity and a need for more nuance than the two legacy codes. A less-breaking design could preserve the primitive field and add richer coding beside it, but that would either fail to make the richer representation the primary base model or create two related mechanism representations with consistency and query costs. Given those material tradeoffs, the alternative is partial and the breaking datatype replacement is probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The main less-breaking base option would keep `AllergyIntolerance.type` as an optional primitive code and introduce a separate optional `CodeableConcept` element for detailed mechanism coding, or profile such detail where needed. That preserves R4 instances but requires mapping and precedence rules when both fields are present and risks long-lived duplicate representations of the allergy/intolerance mechanism. An extension-only approach would be a migration or profiling strategy, not a full base R6 alternative.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 primitive values but leaves the base resource with duplicate mechanism fields and weaker interoperability for systems that only inspect one of them.

evidence.detail: R4 declares `type` as 0..1 `code` with required binding to `ValueSet/allergy-intolerance-type|4.0.1`.
R6 declares `type` as 0..1 `CodeableConcept` with preferred binding to `ValueSet/allergy-intolerance-type`.
Local R4 and R6 CodeSystems both list `allergy` and `intolerance`; the break comes from datatype and binding strength, not an observed code removal.

examples.examplesMd: The R4 primitive value can be wrapped in a CodeableConcept for R6. R6 CodeableConcepts that do not contain a recognizable `allergy` or `intolerance` coding need policy-based or manual mapping to R4.

findings.narrativeMd: `AllergyIntolerance.type` changed from a primitive required-bound code to a CodeableConcept with only a preferred binding. This is both a serialization break and a terminology-conformance widening. Existing R4 JSON such as `"type":"allergy"` cannot be consumed as R6 without transformation.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances with `type` present become invalid in R6 because the JSON value is the wrong type. R6 instances can represent richer or local mechanism concepts that are valid under a preferred binding but cannot be represented in R4's required two-code primitive field without lossy mapping.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Convert R4 `type` to a R6 CodeableConcept using system `http://hl7.org/fhir/allergy-intolerance-type` and the original code. For R6→R4, prefer an explicit coding in that system with code `allergy` or `intolerance`; otherwise define a ConceptMap or manual-review workflow and preserve the original CodeableConcept in an extension if lossless round-trip matters.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The richer datatype is understandable, but it could have been introduced with a parallel extension or staged deprecation. The chosen base element replacement requires all serializers and generated classes to change even when the business value remains one of the two old codes.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `AllergyIntolerance.type` changes from an optional primitive `code` with a required two-code binding to an optional `CodeableConcept` with only a preferred binding, while the short text, definition, and local code system still center on `allergy` versus `intolerance`. This breaks any R4 instance that carries the legacy primitive string and any generated API that models the element as an enum/string. The supplied artifacts do not show a strong enough base-resource rationale for replacing the legacy wire shape rather than preserving it and adding richer mechanism detail separately.
keyEvidence: R4 `AllergyIntolerance.type` is 0..1 primitive `code` with required binding to `ValueSet/allergy-intolerance-type|4.0.1`.
R6 `AllergyIntolerance.type` is 0..1 `CodeableConcept` with preferred binding to `ValueSet/allergy-intolerance-type`.
Both local R4 and R6 `CodeSystem-allergy-intolerance-type` resources contain the same core codes, `allergy` and `intolerance`.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use makes compatibility meaningful for a legacy field the R4 comment explicitly says many systems have captured. The resource is not normative in the supplied R4 context, but the maturity level pushes this hard serialization break toward renewed review.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: a present R4 `type` string such as `allergy` is not the R6 `CodeableConcept` object shape; R6 preferred-bound text or non-legacy codings are also lossy or invalid when converted back to R4.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Yes. A less-breaking base design could retain the primitive `type` for the legacy allergy/intolerance distinction and add an optional `CodeableConcept` detail element for richer mechanism coding. That has some consistency/search cost, but it avoids invalidating legacy instances and better separates the binary legacy classification from richer mechanistic assertions.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: agree that this is a high-impact hard shape break, but disagree that the less-breaking alternative is only a weak partial mitigation; preserving the legacy primitive plus adding richer detail appears plausible enough to merit Revisit.

findings.title: verificationStatus required binding appears to add `presumed`

oldState.summary: R4 verificationStatus is a CodeableConcept with required binding whose visible local code list is unconfirmed, confirmed, refuted, entered-in-error.

binding.description: Assertion about certainty associated with a propensity, or potential risk, of a reaction to the identified substance.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: R4 local CodeSystem has four codes: unconfirmed, confirmed, refuted, entered-in-error.

flags.isModifierReason: This element is labeled as a modifier because the status contains the codes refuted and entered-in-error that mark the AllergyIntolerance as not currently valid.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 does not expose a `presumed` verification status in the local CodeSystem or element short text.

newState.summary: R6 verificationStatus remains required-bound CodeableConcept, and the element short text plus ConceptMap include `presumed`.

binding.description: Assertion about certainty associated with a propensity, or potential risk, of a reaction to the identified substance.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The R6 core package did not include the terminology.hl7.org CodeSystem or an expansion. `presumed` is inferred from the R6 StructureDefinition short text and R6 ConceptMap entry mapping it to resource-status `draft`.

flags.isModifierReason: This element is labeled as a modifier because the status contains the codes refuted and entered-in-error that mark the AllergyIntolerance as not currently valid.

semanticText.definition: Assertion about certainty associated with the propensity, or potential risk, of a reaction to the identified substance (including pharmaceutical product).  The verification status pertains to the allergy or intolerance, itself, not to any specific AllergyIntolerance attribute.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 appears to add `presumed` while keeping the binding required.

facts.note: Inferred from R6 short text and ConceptMap; expansion not available.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The same element and required binding remain, but the visible R6 status list includes an additional code.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 verification-status codes remain valid in R6, so this is not an R4-to-R6 instance break. However, an R6 instance using required-bound `presumed` will fail R4 validation and can break R4 enum switches or status mapping code that only knows the four R4 codes.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Verification status controls whether the allergy assertion is trusted, disputed, or erroneous; an unmapped intermediate status can affect clinical display and decision support.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent an intermediate certainty state between unconfirmed and confirmed.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: adding `presumed` appears to widen the required verification-status value set without removing R4 verification-status codes.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: This finding is not an old-valid/new-invalid R4-to-R6 break: the visible R4 verification-status codes remain available, while R6 appears to add an intermediate `presumed` state. The inferred goal of representing a certainty level between unconfirmed and confirmed is reasonable, though the verdict remains probable because the local package lacks an authoritative expansion or R6 CodeSystem resource.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No backward-compatible base alternative is needed to preserve R4 instances because existing R4 status codes are not removed. Representing `presumed` only in an extension or mapping it to `unconfirmed` would reduce R6-to-R4 friction, but that is a down-conversion mitigation and would make the new R6 certainty state less computable in the base terminology.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R6-to-R4 down-conversion and closed-enum handling still need policy, but preserving R4 instances does not require a less-breaking base R6 design.

evidence.detail: R4 short text lists `unconfirmed | confirmed | refuted | entered-in-error`; binding is required to the R4 versioned value set.
R6 short text lists `unconfirmed | presumed | confirmed | refuted | entered-in-error`; binding remains required to the R6 versioned value set.
R6 ConceptMap includes source code `presumed` mapped to resource-status `draft`.
The R4 local CodeSystem lists four codes and does not include `presumed`; the R6 core package did not include this CodeSystem locally.

migrationExampleJson._migrationNote: Example lossy fallback only; preserve original `presumed` in an extension or require manual review if semantics matter.

examples.examplesMd: The fallback to `unconfirmed` is illustrative, not prescribed. A local ConceptMap or policy decision is needed before collapsing `presumed`.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 appears to add `presumed` to the required verification-status value set. This is not a forward validation break for R4 data, but it is a cross-version and runtime risk for systems with R4-era required-binding enums or logic that assumes the four R4 verification states.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R6 instance using `verificationStatus=presumed` is valid under the R6 required binding if the inferred code membership is confirmed, but it is not valid under R4's required binding. R4 parsers that model verification status as a closed enum may reject or map it to unknown.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Confirm the R6 terminology expansion from terminology.hl7.org. For R6→R4, define a ConceptMap or policy for `presumed`, likely to an extension-preserved original plus a lossy R4 status such as `unconfirmed` if needed. Test enum handling and clinical display for unknown status codes.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Adding a code to a required value set is disruptive for older consumers. An extension would have avoided closed-enum breaks, but it would also make the intermediate certainty state less interoperable in R6.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The local R6 package lacked the underlying terminology.hl7.org CodeSystem and expansions; verify against the authoritative terminology package before final publication.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 appears to add `presumed` to the required verification-status value set while preserving the R4 statuses. This is not an old-valid/new-invalid R4-to-R6 break, but it is a real cross-version and closed-enum issue: an R6 allergy marked `presumed` will not satisfy the R4 required value set and may not map cleanly for clinical logic that distinguishes unconfirmed, confirmed, refuted, and entered-in-error. The intermediate certainty state is clinically plausible, and representing it directly in the required value set is more interoperable than hiding it in an extension.
keyEvidence: R4 `verificationStatus` is 0..1 `CodeableConcept` with required binding; R4 short text lists `unconfirmed | confirmed | refuted | entered-in-error`.
R6 `verificationStatus` remains 0..1 `CodeableConcept` with required binding; R6 short text lists `unconfirmed | presumed | confirmed | refuted | entered-in-error`.
R6 `ConceptMap-sc-allergyintolerance-verification` includes source code `presumed` mapped to canonical resource status `draft`.
The local R6 core package includes the ValueSet but not the underlying THO CodeSystem expansion, so the code-membership evidence is strong but not a full local expansion check.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use increases caution because verification status is modifier-like clinical certainty content. It does not make the additive code suspect by itself, since no R4 code is removed and the clinical need for an intermediate state is understandable.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: R4 instances remain acceptable in R6, but R6 instances using `presumed` fail R4 required-binding validation and can break R4-era closed enum switches or status mappings.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Not applicable for R4-to-R6 preservation. Existing R4 codes are not removed. Using an extension or mapping `presumed` to `unconfirmed` would reduce down-conversion friction but would make the R6 certainty state less computable and less interoperable.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: agree with the reverse-compatibility/runtime risk and the absence of an R4-to-R6 hard break; the impact is best framed as proportionate rather than a design problem needing revisit.

findings.title: R4 clinicalStatus conditional SHALL constraints were removed

oldState.summary: R4 has local root invariants requiring clinicalStatus except when verificationStatus is entered-in-error, and forbidding clinicalStatus when verificationStatus is entered-in-error.

constraints.human: AllergyIntolerance.clinicalStatus SHALL be present if verificationStatus is not entered-in-error.
AllergyIntolerance.clinicalStatus SHALL NOT be present if verification Status is entered-in-error

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 validators enforce the relationship between `verificationStatus` and `clinicalStatus`.

newState.summary: R6 removes the local `ait-1` and `ait-2` error invariants; related guidance is present only in the clinicalStatus comment and accounts for negated allergy codes.

semanticText.comment: AllergyIntolerance.clinicalStatus should be present if verificationStatus is not entered-in-error and the AllergyIntolerance.code isn't negated (No Known Allergy, No Drug Allergy, No Food Allergy, No Latex Allergy).

newState.narrativeMd: R6 no longer enforces these conditions as base validation errors.

facts.note: Removed from R6 local root constraints.
Removed from R6 local root constraints.

facts.oldValue: clinicalStatus required unless verificationStatus is entered-in-error
facts.newValue: clinicalStatus should be present unless entered-in-error and code is not negated
facts.note: Computable SHALL became non-computable guidance with an added negated-code exception.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R4 local constraint keys are absent from the R6 root element; inherited dom/ele constraints were ignored.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Constraint removal is forward-permissive for R4 data, but R6 can now contain instances that R4 rejects: for example, a non-entered-in-error verification status without `clinicalStatus`, or entered-in-error with `clinicalStatus` present. It also changes business-rule assumptions for systems that relied on base validation to enforce status consistency.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Clinical status indicates whether an allergy is active, inactive, or resolved. Missing or inconsistent status can affect filtering and clinical display, especially for safety-sensitive allergy lists.

justification.inferredGoal: Permit negated allergy statements and other special cases where clinicalStatus should not be required by a universal base invariant.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: removing the R4 `ait-1` and `ait-2` error invariants relaxes base validation and does not invalidate R4 instances.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 comment explicitly accounts for negated allergy statements, showing why the R4 unconditional error invariants were too broad. Because the change is forward-permissive, it is not a breaking R4-to-R6 base-design issue even though it creates reverse-version and business-rule risks. The relaxation is therefore probably justified, with the main concern being loss of computable guidance rather than preservation of old instances.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A warning-level or terminology-aware invariant could preserve more machine guidance, but it is not needed to keep R4 instances valid in R6 because the R6 base already relaxes the R4 constraints. Profiles, best-practice warnings, or R6-to-R4 conversion rules may be appropriate mitigations for status consistency, but they are not backward-compatible alternatives to an old-valid/new-invalid base break.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R6 gains flexibility for negated and exceptional cases but loses machine-enforced status consistency; stricter R4 down-conversion needs local validation policy.

evidence.detail: R4 root has local error constraints `ait-1` and `ait-2` governing clinicalStatus presence.
R6 root has no `ait-1` or `ait-2`; only inherited DomainResource constraints remain.
R6 comment says clinicalStatus should be present if verificationStatus is not entered-in-error and the code is not negated.

migrationExampleJson._migrationNote: Only add clinicalStatus when clinically justified; negated allergy statements may need a different policy.

examples.examplesMd: The R6 example omits `clinicalStatus` with a non-entered-in-error verification status. That is allowed by the R6 base StructureDefinition but violates R4 `ait-1`.

findings.narrativeMd: R4 had two AllergyIntolerance-specific error invariants tying `clinicalStatus` to `verificationStatus`; R6 removes them. The removal is not an R4→R6 validation break, but it is a semantic and conformance shift because R6 base validation no longer guarantees the same status consistency that R4 validators enforced.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Existing R4-valid data remains acceptable with respect to these constraints. The risk is reverse compatibility and business logic: R6-valid instances can fail R4 validation, and systems that inferred `clinicalStatus` would always be present except for entered-in-error records must handle missing status and negated-code exceptions.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R6→R4, evaluate `verificationStatus`, `clinicalStatus`, and negated allergy codes together. Do not blindly synthesize `clinicalStatus`; where conversion to R4 is required, either add a clinically correct status, use an extension/profile exception, or reject/manual-review cases where the R6 semantics intentionally omit status. Keep regression tests for confirmed-without-clinicalStatus and entered-in-error-with-clinicalStatus cases.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The broad R4 invariant was probably too rigid for negated allergy statements, so relaxing it is understandable. A warning-level invariant or more specific computable rule would have preserved more machine guidance while avoiding hard rejection, but terminology-dependent negation makes that hard to do reliably in the base resource.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Reviewers should confirm whether the intended normative behavior is fully captured by prose or by profiles elsewhere in the R6 ballot.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 enforced two root-level error invariants tying `clinicalStatus` presence to `verificationStatus`; R6 removes those hard constraints and replaces part of the rule with prose saying clinical status should be present unless the assertion is entered-in-error or the code is negated. This does not invalidate existing R4 instances, but it changes validation expectations and permits R6 instances that will fail R4 validation or surprise systems that relied on the base invariant. The relaxation appears proportionate because the old invariant was too broad for negated allergy statements, though implementers may still need profile or business-rule validation for safety-sensitive allergy lists.
keyEvidence: R4 root `AllergyIntolerance` has local error constraints `ait-1` and `ait-2` requiring clinicalStatus unless verificationStatus is entered-in-error and forbidding clinicalStatus for entered-in-error.
R6 root `AllergyIntolerance` no longer contains `ait-1` or `ait-2`; only inherited DomainResource constraints are present in the extracted root constraints.
R6 `AllergyIntolerance.clinicalStatus.comment` says clinicalStatus should be present if verificationStatus is not entered-in-error and the AllergyIntolerance.code is not negated.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use raises the burden because clinical status affects active/resolved allergy interpretation, but the change is forward-permissive and the new prose identifies a clinical exception. The maturity context supports careful migration guidance rather than a Revisit judgment.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: R6 can now contain combinations that R4 validators reject; there is also a semantic/documentation shift because base validation no longer enforces the status consistency rule.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Partial. A best-practice warning or a terminology-aware invariant could preserve more computable guidance without restoring the overbroad R4 hard error, but negated allergy detection is terminology-dependent and hard to express safely in the base resource. Profiles remain a better place for stricter local policy.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing report correctly treats this as not an R4-to-R6 hard break, with meaningful reverse/business-rule risk and no simple fully backward-compatible base alternative.

findings.title: AllergyIntolerance.recorder can now reference Organization

oldState.summary: R4 recorder references Practitioner, PractitionerRole, Patient, or RelatedPerson.

semanticText.definition: Individual who recorded the record and takes responsibility for its content.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 limits recorder to individual or role-like actors.

newState.summary: R6 recorder adds Organization as an allowed reference target and clarifies recorder as the most recent author responsible for accurate recording.

semanticText.definition: Individual who recorded the record and takes responsibility for accurately recording its content.
semanticText.comment: Because the recorder takes responsibility for accurately recording information in the record, the recorder is the most recent author.  The recorder might or might not be the asserter.  By contrast, the recordedDate is when the allergy or intolerance was first recorded.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 allows an organization to be the recorder and clarifies that recorder represents the most recent author rather than necessarily the first recorder.

facts.newValue: Recorder is the most recent author and may differ from asserter.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The same element id/path and cardinality remain; one targetProfile and explanatory text were added.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 data remains valid in R6 because the target set widened. R6 instances with `recorder` pointing to `Organization` violate the R4 target profile and may not fit R4 generated model constraints or business logic expecting a person or role.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Recorder provenance affects audit and attribution more than allergy clinical meaning, but incorrect attribution can still matter for data governance.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent institutional authorship or responsibility for recording allergy information.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: adding `Organization` widens the `recorder` target set while preserving all R4 recorder target types.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal of representing institutional recording responsibility is plausible, and the R6 definition/comment clarifies recorder as the most recent author responsible for accurate recording. Since no R4 target profile is removed, the change preserves R4 instances and the remaining costs are closed-union code updates and R6-to-R4 representability.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No less-breaking base alternative is needed for R4-to-R6 preservation: the R6 target list is a superset of R4. Using `Provenance.agent` or an extension for organization attribution could help R4 down-conversion, but that is a migration mitigation for R6-only content rather than an alternative to a breaking R6 base design.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R6-only Organization recorders require down-conversion, Provenance, or extension policy, but the base widening does not make R4 instances invalid.

evidence.detail: R4 target profiles are Practitioner, PractitionerRole, Patient, and RelatedPerson.
R6 adds Organization to the recorder target profile list.
R6 clarifies recorder as most recent author and distinguishes it from recordedDate and asserter.

migrationExampleJson._migrationNote: If no person/role equivalent exists, preserve the Organization recorder in Provenance or an extension rather than forcing an inaccurate person reference.

examples.examplesMd: The migration example intentionally does not invent a person recorder. R4 conversion may need companion Provenance or an extension for fidelity.

findings.narrativeMd: `recorder` now allows `Organization`. This is a widening change for R6 and does not invalidate R4 instances, but it creates reverse-compatibility failures for R4 validators and generated clients when an R6 AllergyIntolerance records an institutional author.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4→R6 validation is safe for existing target types. R6→R4 conversion is not lossless for Organization recorders unless there is a known individual/role proxy or an extension/Provenance strategy. Runtime code that switches on target resource type must handle Organization.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Update R6 clients and server validation to allow `Organization` as `recorder`. For R6→R4, prefer preserving organization attribution in `Provenance` or an agreed extension; only map to PractitionerRole or Practitioner when there is a semantically accurate target. Add target-type tests for all five R6 recorder target profiles.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The added target is clinically plausible and probably justified. It could have been modeled through Provenance alone, but making it a direct target improves base resource usability while requiring R4 adapters to handle a new actor type.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `recorder` keeps the same path, cardinality, and existing R4 reference targets, and R6 only adds `Organization`. Existing R4 instances remain valid against this aspect of R6. R6-only organization recorders need down-conversion policy for R4, but the practical concern is mostly attribution/audit handling rather than a forward compatibility break in allergy clinical content.
keyEvidence: R4 `AllergyIntolerance.recorder` targets Practitioner, PractitionerRole, Patient, and RelatedPerson.
R6 `AllergyIntolerance.recorder` retains those targets and adds Organization.
R6 recorder prose clarifies the recorder as the most recent author responsible for accurate recording.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use does not turn a target-list widening into a standards concern. The added target affects reverse exchange and audit modeling, but it preserves the mature R4 target set.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: only R6 instances using an Organization recorder fail the R4 target profile; there is no old-valid/new-invalid R4-to-R6 break.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Not applicable. The R6 base target set is a superset of R4. Provenance or an extension may help R4 down-conversion, but that is migration policy rather than a less-breaking R6 base design.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: agree with the reverse-compatibility observation, but the existing medium-impact framing overstates the R4-to-R6 concern for an additive target widening with likely low practical risk.
